newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ARSENAL AND VILLA HOPE TO BOUNCE BACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ARSENAL AND VILLA HOPE TO BOUNCE BACK.

text.p: Title-chasing Arsenal and Aston Villa will both be looking to bounce back from disappointing results when they meet at Highbury on Saturday.

Arsenal were held to a disappointing 0-0 draw with Sheffield Wednesday at Hillsborough on Boxing Day while Aston Villa's run of five successive league wins came to a halt when they were beaten 2-0 at home by Chelsea.
Despite those scorelines, both teams believe they can still win the title in the most open English league championship race for years.
And if Arsenal win by 2-0 or more on Saturday they will go back on top of the table -- at least until Sunday when current leaders Liverpool play at Southampton.
Arsenal are now second, three points behind Liverpool, and boast the only unbeaten home record in the premier league.

Villa beat Wimbledon 5-0 last Sunday to move into fourth place after chalking up their fifth successive league win but they slipped back to fifth after losing to Chelsea who got two Christmas gift-wrapped goals as presents from Villa 'keeper Mark Bosnich.
Villa go to Highbury six points behind Liverpool but if they beat Arsenal and other results go their way they could be as high as third by Saturday night.
Manager Brian Little has three doubtful players and could be without Yugoslav striker Savo Milosevic (virus) and midfielders Mark Draper (groin) and Ian Taylor (knee).
Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger's one main doubt is former Villa skipper David Platt who is nursing a hamstring injury and may not be fit to face one of his former clubs.

First-choice goalkeeper David Seaman is near to full fitness after breaking three ribs against Manchester United in November but John Lukic is expected to continue to deputise for him while Lee Dixon has still not recovered from an ankle injury.

Arsenal's squad may be older than most of their rivals -- all four regular defenders and Seaman are over 30 -- but the vast experience of players such as skipper Tony Adams, Platt, Dennis Bergkamp and Ian Wright is paying dividends in pressure situations.
Arsenal tend to grind out draws from matches that other teams may lose and they snatch victories from games that look like ending level.

They did it against Aston Villa earlier in the season when they pulled back from 2-0 down with late goals from Paul Merson and Andy Linighan to salvage a 2-2 draw. They did it against arch-rivals Tottenham to win 3-1 last month with two goals in the last two minutes and they ground out a 2-1 victory at Newcastle despite playing for 70 minutes with only 10 men after Adams was sent off.
Wenger has given Arsenal a new attacking dimension to their play and with Wright, who has hit 21 goals already this season, in such excellent form, they are always likely to score.

The downside for Arsenal is the temperament of some of their players. They are currently bottom in the unofficial fair play league having picked up 41 bookings and two red cards this season. Wright, who was sent off against Forest last Saturday, could miss five matches in January if he is booked again during the busy holiday programme.
Like Arsenal, Aston Villa are capable of scoring from a number of positions and their 5-0 rout of Wimbledon included two from Milosevic, two from Dwight Yorke and one from Taylor.
Two years after taking over, Little has forged a team that reached the semifinals of the F.A. Cup last season, won the League Cup and on their day are a handful for any other team.

The two clubs are traditionally among the front-runners with trophies regularly decorating their boardrooms. Villa won the League Cup in both 1994 and last season, while Arsenal have won the League, the F.A. Cup, the League Cup and the European Cup Winners Cup in the 1990s and both are among the elite group of six clubs to have performed the English League and Cup double.
This season marks the 100th anniversary of Villa's double in 1896-97, while Arsenal emulated that performance in 1971.
Neither squad looks strong enough to repeat such a feat this season -- but both look capable of picking up at least one major honour in six months' time.
Teams:

Arsenal (from): John Lukic; Martin Keown, Tony Adams, Steve Bould, Scott Marshall, Nigel Winterburn, Ray Parlour, Remi Garde, Patrick Vieira, Paul Merson, David Platt, Paul Shaw, Dennis Bergkamp, Ian Wright.

Aston Villa (from): Mark Bosnich; Ugo Ehiogu, Alan Wright, Steve Staunton, Riccardo Scimeca, Fernando Nelson, Ian Taylor, Mark Draper, Sasa Curcic, Andy Townsend, Dwight Yorke, Savo Milosevic, Tommy Johnson.
